_doc: A/B test plan for @itsongit. pipeline/plan.py assigns arms per day, pipeline/experiments.py reports. Reels before 'started' are the baseline (all hook=price).

windows.why: 11-12h Berlin: 10 reels, median 100+ views (best median of any hour band)
18-19h: 9 reels, mean 119 (best mean); studies agree early evening is strong for Reels
20-23h median only ~25, but the Mixxx breakout (22:48) landed here and studies favour 8 PM-midnight: kept as the measured third window

dropped_windows.13:00-14:59: 16 reels, median 33-44 views: the dead zone (moved later, to the evening)
dropped_windows.07:00-09:00: never tested; candidate for the next window test if night stays weak

hook.question: Does showing the app in action on frame 0 cut the 3-second skip rate?

arms.price: A: HyperFrames price-slash text card (control, every reel so far)
arms.demo: B: app-in-action cold open, job line on top, struck price strip below (same voiceover)

hook.decide: B wins if its median skip rate is at least 5 points lower than A's AND its median views are not lower. A wins if B is not better after 15 per arm. Then make the winner the default and test the next hook idea against it.

topic.question: Which kind of 'everyone pays for this' pick travels furthest?

arms.subscription: replaces a famous monthly/yearly subscription (Adobe, Canva, Grammarly, Office…)
arms.utility: desktop/phone utility that fixes a daily annoyance (Magnet, Paste, CleanMyMac…)
arms.hobby: creative/hobby tool where the paid app is famous in that hobby (Serato, Photoshop…)

topic.decide: After 10 per arm, give the best arm 2 of the 3 daily reels; keep 1 rotating so the others keep being measured.
topic.banned: developer, academic and pro-only tools (the 'niche' baseline group: median views far below the rest)

windows_note: Analysed by real Berlin posting time. The old slot numbers only picked the accent colour (times were already randomised).
